change.author: nicktrn

findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password check when any totpCode is sent
findings.body: In `authorize`, the password is verified only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). Any non-empty `totpCode` skips that check, and the backup-code branch at line 131 then accepts `backupCode` alone. A request with the email, a valid backup code and any `totpCode` value (for example "0") logs in without the password. The same gate already lets email plus a valid TOTP skip the password (this is pre-existing), but backup codes are static and stay valid until used, so this adds a longer-lived single-factor credential. The disable endpoint does the right thing: it verifies the password before the backup branch (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:40-45). Fix: in the backup branch, verify `credentials.password` against `user.password` when the user has one, before a code is consumed. Also confirm whether the pre-existing TOTP gate at line 121 is intended.

findings.title: Backup code can be spent twice under concurrent logins
findings.body: The code is checked at line 144 and the remaining list is written back in a separate update (lines 149-156) with no condition on the value read. Two concurrent credential requests with the same code can both pass the `indexOf` check and both succeed, so one code is used twice. The UI copy says each code "can be used exactly once" (apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json:2015). Make the consumption atomic, for example an `updateMany` conditioned on the stored value, and reject when the count is 0.

findings.title: Dismissing the backup-codes step with Escape or outside click loses the codes and leaves the UI showing 2FA disabled
findings.body: The codes are shown only in the DisplayBackupCodes step, and that step closes through the Close button, which calls `onEnable` (lines 266-270). `onEnable` is what closes the parent and refreshes the switch (apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64-68). Escape or a click outside reaches the Radix dialog's `onOpenChange` (packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx:87-104). The parent turns it into a plain toggle (two-factor-auth.tsx:64) and never calls `onEnable`. At that point the server already has 2FA enabled (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable.ts:61), the switch still shows Disabled, and no endpoint returns the codes again, so after a reload they cannot be seen. Handle dismissal in the DisplayBackupCodes step the same way as Close, or ignore dismissal until the codes are acknowledged.

findings.title: Switch assertion is vacuous: expect() receives a Promise
findings.body: `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to `expect`, so it can never fail. That is why the FIXME above it (lines 50-51) says the check passes when the switch is off. Use `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()`, or the `data-state="checked"` locator already used at line 127.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup code in lost-access mode does nothing visible
findings.body: In lost-access mode the form is `noValidate` (line 188), so the `required` BackupCode input is not enforced and an empty value is sent. `authorize` treats an empty string as no backup code and falls through to the TOTP branch (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:157-159), which throws SecondFactorRequired. Line 156 sets the same state again and shows no message, so the submit appears to do nothing. Show an error for an empty backup code.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes points users to a settings action that does not exist
findings.body: "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Settings sits behind login, and there is no generate action: codes are created only by disabling and re-enabling 2FA, which needs a TOTP code or a backup code. Accounts that enabled 2FA before this migration have NULL `backupCodes` (packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 adds the column with no backfill), so they see this message with no way to act on it. Reword the copy and decide how these accounts recover.

findings.title: Copy button reports success even when the clipboard write fails
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast on the next line runs regardless. If the write is rejected, the user sees "Backup codes copied!" and gets an unhandled promise rejection. Await the write inside try/catch and show the toast only on success.

findings.title: tabIndex=-1 on the password reveal button applies to every PasswordField
findings.body: This removes the show/hide control from the keyboard tab order for every PasswordField, including login.tsx:203, EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:174 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:94 and the other consumers. The PR body says it is intentional ("make password visible tooltip non-tabbable"). Keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password they typed. Consider keeping the button focusable and fixing the tooltip, or scoping the change to the 2FA fields.

findings.title: Backup codes are matched case-sensitively and without trimming
findings.body: The input is compared after removing dashes only (line 144). Codes are lowercase hex (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:61), so a code typed in uppercase, or pasted with surrounding spaces, is rejected as incorrect. The same comparison is in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61. Lowercasing and trimming before the match would fix both.

contracts.action: Backup-code login through the credentials provider
contracts.before_after: TOTP branch requires totpCode, checks secret length and runs totpAuthenticatorCheck. Backup branch checks the encryption key, decrypts the list, matches the code, nulls the used entry and writes the list back in a separate update. Neither branch calls verifyPassword when totpCode is non-empty (line 121 gate).
contracts.visible_effect: Login succeeds, or login.tsx shows the mapped error message.
contracts.failure_mode: Password is not checked when totpCode is non-empty (line 121), so a backup code alone logs in. Concurrent requests with the same code can both succeed (no conditional update, lines 144-156).

contracts.before_after: Password is verified first for CAL users (lines 40-45). The backup branch does not consume the code (comment at line 66). All codes are cleared on success (line 107).
contracts.visible_effect: Modal shows the mapped error, or closes and invalidates the user query on success.
contracts.failure_mode: Missing backup codes return 400 MissingBackupCodes, which the modal maps to a message. A non-string backupCode throws at line 61 and becomes a generic 500. Not user-visible in a harmful way.

contracts.before_after: Before the change, handleEnable called onEnable() on a successful enable, which closed the dialog and invalidated viewer.me. Now handleEnable moves to DisplayBackupCodes and onEnable() runs only from the Close button.
contracts.visible_effect: The switch keeps showing Disabled until Close is pressed.
contracts.failure_mode: Escape or outside click calls the parent's toggle without onEnable. The server has 2FA enabled while the UI shows it disabled, and the codes are never shown again after a reload.

contracts.action: Generate and persist backup codes during setup
contracts.before_after: The codes are written next to the secret while twoFactorEnabled stays false. The list is overwritten on every setup call. The codes are returned at line 78.
contracts.visible_effect: Codes are returned to the modal and shown after enable.
contracts.failure_mode: If the user abandons setup, the stored codes are unused and are overwritten by the next setup. No visible effect.

contracts.action: Lost-access toggle in the disable modal
contracts.before_after: The toggle swaps TwoFactor for BackupCode and clears the code fields. The Button defaults to type=button, so it does not submit the form.
contracts.visible_effect: The input swaps and the label changes to Go back.

contracts.action: Lost-access toggle on the login page
contracts.before_after: Sets the flag and clears totpCode. Go back clears backupCode and resets the flag.
contracts.visible_effect: The BackupCode input renders in place of TwoFactor (login.tsx:221).
contracts.failure_mode: An empty submit is silently a no-op (next-auth-options.ts:157-159, login.tsx:156, form noValidate at line 188).
The clipboard promise is neither awaited nor caught (line 278), so the toast shows even when the write fails.

contracts.before_after: New action with no sibling. The Button inside the anchor defaults to type=button.

contracts.equivalent_path: apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:213 (tabIndex -1 on the forgot-password link, a different element)
contracts.before_after: The reveal button was in the tab order. It is now tabIndex -1 for every PasswordField.
contracts.failure_mode: Keyboard-only users cannot reach the reveal control. The PR body says this is intentional.

summary: Read-only review of the 16 files in part 1. The backup-code login path has a blocker: the password check is skipped whenever a non-empty totpCode is sent, so email plus a valid backup code logs in without the password (next-auth-options.ts:121, 131). Also: backup codes can be spent twice under concurrent logins (next-auth-options.ts:144-156); dismissing the backup-codes step with Escape or outside click loses the codes and leaves the UI showing 2FA disabled (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:166); and the 2FA switch e2e assertion is vacuous (login.2fa.e2e.ts:53). The rest are consider-level: copy and clipboard handling, the empty-submit no-op, the stale missing-codes copy for pre-migration accounts, the global tabIndex change to PasswordField (intentional per the PR body), and case and whitespace normalisation of codes. Nothing was built or run.
